svg.text: MeetHalfway AI: Fair, Real-Time, Explainable Meeting-Place Recommendation
A competition-style poster for a Streamlit + Python decision-support system that helps two people find a practical halfway venue
Core idea: travel-time fairness + live venue signals + explainable ranking
Repository basis: README, app_streamlit.py, app_streamlit_new.py, meethalfway.py

text.tspan: Meeting halfway is usually handled badly: people eyeball a midpoint,
ignore travel-time asymmetry, and still need to manually check whether
a place is open, crowded, or practical.
turns this into an explainable recommendation workflow.
Instead of a naive geographic midpoint, it computes a fair reachable zone
from two users, retrieves candidates, enriches them with live signals,
and ranks venues with a transparent scoring breakdown.

svg.text: Fairness is based on travel-time intersection, not visual midpoint.
Candidates are adjusted by open/closed, queue, crowd, risk.
Ranking remains explainable instead of black-box only.
Strong engineering fallback chain keeps the demo stable.
1. Collect two user locations and preferences
3. Search venue candidates near fair center
4. Enrich with live web signals and semantics
• User coordinates are intended for in-session processing only.
• `room_state.json` stores collaboration state for the richer app flow.
• API instability is handled with retries and graceful fallbacks.
• Search fallback chain: Mapbox → Overpass → OSM.
• Semantic fallback chain: OpenAI-compatible model → keyword extraction.
Streamlit UI + interactive map + top picks + surprise mode
A/B users provide address, GPS, time slots, budget, votes
Session state, invite links, room join, vote persistence,
candidate search, web enrichment, scoring, explanations
Folium map, cards, result pages, surprise recommendation
Place Search: Mapbox POI → Overpass → OSM
Goal: the demo still works even if one API is missing.
Retrieval: Mapbox, Overpass, OSM, Tavily, DuckDuckGo
Address or GPS is converted into lat/lon
Step B. Estimate a weighted midpoint
Bias can shift the center toward a tired or constrained user
Step C. Compute fair overlap area
Isochrone(A) ∩ Isochrone(B) = region both can reach reasonably
Step D. Search nearby venue candidates
Prioritize the overlap centroid, then retain safe fallbacks
Step E. Enrich each venue with live signals
Status, queue risk, crowd level, wait estimate, confidence
Blend distance, rating proxy, fairness, voting, availability, risk
Top picks, surprise pick, reasons, and map markers
Final Score = distance + rating + fairness + spatiotemporal bonus
minus closure / queue / risk penalties, plus isochrone reward
Uses travel-time gap rather than pure kilometer distance.
Queue level and estimated wait time
Crowd index, promo bonus, risk penalty
Venue type • budget • travel mode • time slots
Interactive map preview with overlap area and venue pins
small travel-time gap + inside overlap + manageable crowd
• Recommendation is not just “closest to center”.
• It also reflects whether both users can realistically get there.
• Risky venues are downgraded even if they look central.
• The UI can show rankings, votes, confidence, and map markers.
• `app_streamlit_new.py` adds room logic, local storage, vote flow, and
• `meethalfway.py` is the real engine: geocoding, fairness zone, place
retrieval, enrichment, scoring, explanations, and map generation.
• The architecture is essentially a competition-ready Python monolith
with strong fallback behavior and clear demoability.
This is a practical decision-support system,

MeetHalfway AI reframes “where should we meet?” as a fairness-aware, real-time, and explainable optimization problem. The project combines geo reachability, fallback-first engineering, live web signals, and interpretable scoring into a demo-ready product experience.
Poster style adapted from the reference competition slide: dark blue academic header, white research-poster layout, modular column sections, and figure-first storytelling.
